rubric.evidence: Live check on 2026-11-27 of https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Supports-Loading-Mode (HTTP 200, index.json inspected): MDN's Directives section lists ONLY `credentialed-prerender` and `fenced-frame` and does NOT document `prerender-cross-origin-frames`. The stub's prose ('MDN covers the full set of tokens, including prerender-cross-origin-frames') is currently inaccurate.
H1 'Prerendering cross-origin iframes' matches Chrome 147 listing; declared ChromeStatus row links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5112398709129216; notes Origin trial Chrome 147-152.

Status is `stub` ('covered on mdn'), but the linked MDN Supports-Loading-Mode page does not actually cover the `prerender-cross-origin-frames` token yet. The page does include inline 'at a glance', 'why it exists', 'how it works', and 'browser support' sections, so upgrading it to a full `built` reference (with reference-contract.json) or correcting the MDN coverage claim is needed.
Explains the shell-architecture motivation, page-B response header placement, document.prerendering/prerenderingchange behavior inside cross-origin frames, and memory/battery heuristics clearly.
Provides HTTP header examples for standalone and combined `Supports-Loading-Mode: credentialed-prerender, prerender-cross-origin-frames` in <pre><code> (lacks tabindex='0').
Includes an Origin trial warning callout (Chrome 147-152 desktop + Android), flag name `prerender2-cross-origin-iframes`, and a 4-browser support table sourced to ChromeStatus.

Live check on 2026-11-27: MDN Supports-Loading-Mode returns direct HTTP 200; CPS demo URL https://chrome-platform-showcase.kinlan-test.workers.dev/v147/prerendering-cross-origin-iframes/ returns HTTP 200 (the parenthetical '(when built)' text next to the link is now stale). All external links carry target='_blank' rel='noopener' and citations are directly linked.
Single <main>, single <h1>, sequential h2 headings, and semantic lists. Minor legacy gaps: both .doc-table elements omit <caption>/<th scope='row'>, and <pre> omits tabindex='0'.

Uses /public/styles.css tokens (var(--border-black), var(--bg-stone), var(--thin-shadow), var(--font-mono)) and viewport meta; recorded desktop:ok and mobile:ok in responsive-support.json (2026-10-10 headless-Chrome audit).
